title: Onboarding Accelerator: Cross-Pod Playbook & 30-60-90 Buddy Rotation
body:
Purpose:
This playbook outlines a lightweight, repeatable cross-pod onboarding accelerator aimed at shortening time-to-contribution for new ICs (engineers, infra, product ops) by combining focused first-week bootcamp sessions with a rotating buddy system across 3 pods.

Scope & when to use:
- Use for new ICs joining engineering-adjacent roles and early IC hires in product/infra where cross-team context speeds ramp.
- Not intended for high-compliance private deployments hires (see private-deployments/onboarding).

Goals (metric-aligned):
- Week 1: new hire completes two small shipped tasks (docs, infra smoke test, or simple bugfix) with buddy support.
- 30 days: first meaningful PR/feature/instrumentation merged and owner assigned.
- 90 days: full ownership of one micro-scope (e.g., feature area or infra surface), measured by ownership ticket and on-call readiness checklist.

Why cross-pod buddy rotation? (hypothesis)
- Increases exposure to system boundaries and reduces siloed context.
- Provides multiple short-term mentors so onboarding knowledge isn't single-person dependent.
- Improves lateral network for the new hire (faster follow-up, engineer-to-engineer support).

Prerequisites (people-ops / hiring):
- Hiring packet complete and manager confirmed 2-week plan before start.
- Access requests filed 5 business days prior (GSuite, Slack, repo, CI).
- Bootcamp slots scheduled in calendar for week 1: infra walkthrough, deployment runbook, product orientation.

Stakeholders & roles:
- Hiring manager: owns 30/60/90 plan and assigned micro-scope.
- Primary buddy (pod A): day-to-day shadow for week 1 and async follow-ups.
- Rotating buddies (pod B, pod C): 2-day shadow windows in weeks 2–3.
- People Ops: coordinates access, logistics, and collects feedback at 14/30/90 days.

First-week (detailed playbook — flexible):
Day 0 (prestart checklist):
- Confirm laptop image queued and VPN keys shipped.
- Manager posts welcome note in #onboard and introduces buddy.
- Add to on-call rota read-only if relevant.

Day 1: orientation + small wins
- 09:00 - Team intro + org chart quick walkthrough (manager) (30m).
- 10:00 - Product orientation: 15-min demo + 15-min fuzzy Q&A.
- 11:00 - Workspace setup + repo clone with buddy (pair) (2h).
- Afternoon: small environment-only task (readme fix / lint rule) -> PR and review.

Day 2: infra & CI flows
- Morning: CI pipeline walkthrough and deploy staging runbook (buddy).
- Afternoon: run a pre-approved staging deploy with buddy observing.

Day 3: feature archetype + observability
- Morning: shadow owner pair for feature hotpath (1h).
- Afternoon: add an instrumentation metric or dashboard tile (small ticket).

Day 4: cross-pod rotation (pod B buddy)
- 1-day focused pairing in a nearby pod to review a different code path.

Day 5: reflection + shipping
- AM: complete any blocked PRs + setup retrospective notes.
- PM: 30-min sync with manager to confirm 30-day plan and first micro-scope.

Week 2–4 (concrete checkpoints):
- Rotating buddy windows: 2 days with pod B (week 2), 2 days with pod C (week 3).
- Weekly deliverables: at least 1 merged PR/week increasing in complexity.
- 14-day survey from People Ops (what worked / blockers).

30-60-90 sample milestone map (manager-owned):
- 30d: merged micro-scope + documentation + ownership ticket.
- 60d: independently own a lifecycle (deploy -> monitor -> fix) under light supervision.
- 90d: on-call readiness verified + post-90 plan (career thread).

Mini hiring plan adjustments for cross-pod hires (to include in req brief):
- Candidate profile emphasis: curiosity about systems tradeoffs, evidence of cross-team collaboration.
- Interview loop tweak: add one 45-min "system boundaries" exercise (candidate reads architecture snippet and calls out touchpoints).
- Scorecard changes: add a cross-pod collaboration dimension (scale 1–4).

Sample interview rubric bullets (snippet to paste into panel notes):
- Technical mastery: writes correct, idiomatic code. (1–4)
- System thinking: identifies upstream/downstream impacts; suggests monitoring points. (1–4)
- Collaboration: describes past cross-team work and tradeoff negotiation. (1–4)
- Communication: explains decisions clearly to non-experts. (1–4)
- Ramp potential: how quickly they learn from feedback / shipping small iterations. (1–4)
Notes: default hire if median >=3 and no 1s in system thinking or collaboration.

Onboarding checklist (quick copy for hiring manager):
- Prestart: laptop, network access, Slack + repo invites, calendar blocks for bootcamp.
- Day1: team welcome, clone + build, small PR.
- Week1: deploy to staging, rotate buddies, 14d feedback form.
- 30d: micro-scope ownership ticket + manager checkpoint.
- 90d: on-call cert / ownership review.

Success signals (leading & lagging):
- Leading: number of async help threads the new hire starts/answers, frequency of buddy interactions.
- Lagging: time-to-first-merge (goal <= 10 business days), time-to-oncall-readiness (goal <= 90 days).

Retention risks & mitigations:
- If repeated blocked PRs >7 days -> escalate to manager + people-ops for focused unblock.
- If new hire reports low collaborator interactions -> schedule cross-pod coffee intros and assign another short buddy rotation.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Quantify ideal buddy rotation cadence (2 days vs 3 days) — A/B test with next 6 hires starting Jan–Mar.
- Instrumentation: add onboarding event tags to telemetry so we can compute time-to-first-meaningful-PR automatically.
- Should we require rotating buddies include one senior engineer and one mid-level? pros/cons.

Related artifacts and quick links (copy-paste):
- Confluence playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PE/Onboarding-Accelerator
- 14d feedback form template: HRJIRA-987 -> /forms/onboard-14d
- Slack pilot channel: #onboard-accelerator (used for cohort scheduling)

Appendix: short sample manager email to send before start (paste):
Hi team — joining on MON is {{name}} (role). Primary buddy is {{buddy}}. Please add a 30m intro slot to your calendar this week if you work closely with the infra or deploy flow. Our goal is to get them to ship a small item by Friday. Thanks — Manager

End notes: this is intentionally lightweight and iterative. Treat as minimum viable scaffold — we want to test variations and measure downstream retention and ramp time.
